title: Meter volume figures reported and corrected by hand over email
label_mechanical: Meter data requests and corrections: report volume / meter / data

narrative.what_happens: Someone needs the measured volume at a particular meter for a period, and a colleague pulls the figure and sends it back in the body of an email. Most of the messages are one-way statements of volume for a given meter and period, with a smaller number of replies answering a specific request and at least one instance correcting a volume previously reported for a prior period. In one case the sender offers to forward the underlying statement document separately rather than attaching it, so the number travels in mail while the supporting record stays behind in whatever system produced it. The exchange ends when the requester has the number; no confirmation step back into a system is visible in these messages.
narrative.where_it_stalls: Nothing in this set shows chasing or missed cutoffs — the waiting, rework and deadline signals are all absent. The visible friction is narrower: the volume is retyped into mail rather than read from the source, and the supporting statement is offered on request instead of travelling with the figure, so the recipient holds a number without its provenance. One message correcting a prior period's meter volume suggests figures do get restated after the fact, but on this evidence that is a single occurrence rather than a pattern.
narrative.why_it_recurs: Meter volumes are needed per meter and per period by people who do not have direct access to the measurement records, so each request produces a fresh manual lookup and a fresh email. The occurrences here are scattered across four months rather than tied to a visible cycle.
narrative.automation_opportunity: A self-service lookup that returns volume by meter and period, with the source statement attached automatically, would remove the intermediary from most of these exchanges. Failing that, a standing extract mailed to the regular requesters would pre-empt the one-off asks.

steps: 8.00 task instances / 4 months of coverage = 2.000 instances per month
minutes per instance = 9 handle + (1.12 touches - 1) x 4 + 0.00 rework rate x 12 + 0.00 waiting rate x 3 = 9.50 min
